findings.finding: Opens 'We did not replicate the three simulation headlines of Chen (2021), who reported biased direct-effect estimates, percentile bootstrap intervals that cover the true value far too rarely, and power for the mediated interaction (MINT) near zero', then gives each signed contrast (85.42 vs 0.00; 43.62 vs 0.04; 0.013 vs 0.786). Composite verdict first, source cited.
H4 'holds only in part' with the n = 5,000 shares, and RQ2 'could not be rerun' (blocked, not called a nonreplication) follow immediately; S9 '10 of 15' given.

Limits and explanations stated: unseeded bootstrap, exact replay scope ('replayed on all 1,280,000 datasets it generates'), eight explained / two partly explained disagreements, tolerances and 'not equivalence'.

'We did not replicate the simulation headlines of Chen (2021): her finding that the natural direct effects are biased (85.42% ... 0.00% in ours), ...' Verdict first, independent of the abstract, with locators (Table 4.8, Table 4.9, figure) and numbers.
Evidence limits (Head Start blocked; bootstrap unseeded) in the same paragraph; 'No estimate reverses its sign.' consistent with Table 1.
Explanations kept with their uncertainty: 'Section 6.2, only partly explained'.
Readable without other documents; every abbreviation (PNDE, TNDE, MINT, Bradley's range) is defined in the paper. No reference to earlier drafts or reviews.
Project-internal governance narrative ('without first asking the owner of this replication project', issue numbers) is candid and understandable; polish only.
Orphan heading at the bottom of p21; ledger on p22 uses workflow vocabulary ('preflight', 'check_citations.py'). Polish only.

'The sides differ only in random draws ... and in the step that compares estimates with population values' contradicts Table 2's own Data row ('published results evidently lack h where h > 0'). Should-fix wording; Table 2 directly below corrects it, so not a failing defect.

85.42 = 100 minus mean of six Table 4.8 PNDE/TNDE within-[-.10,.10] values (12.50,12.50,18.75,12.50,12.50,18.75; source-values/table_4_8.csv, source PDF p. 102); ours 0.00 (results/table48_ours.csv, all within 100%). Magnitude smaller, zero vs nonzero correct (ours within tolerance 0.005 of zero).

43.6193 -> 43.62 and 47.0713 -> 47.07 from source-values/table_4_9.csv (printed to two decimals on source p. 138); ours 0.0358 -> 0.04 and 0.3258 -> 0.33 from results/table49_ours.csv; both beyond tolerance, same sign; labels correct.

Published 0.0127 = mean(0.0627, 0.0683, 0.0571) - .05 from results/digitized_rates.csv (Figure 4.28, a = .59, h = .34, n = 500); ours 0.8361 - .05 = 0.786 (results/summary.json). Tolerance 0.01233 recorded as 0.0123 (not rounded up). 0.0127 > 0.0123 so 'same direction'; near-tie and post-hoc tolerance disclosed in caption.
Nonscalar; magnitude/direction 'not established'; verdict 'partial' matches packet partly_replicated.
All 13 packet claims (H1-H4, S1-S9) listed with statuses identical to the packet; claim_map pages verified (e.g. S9 Table 3 on page 10, H4 Section 6.8 on page 15).

S2/S3 counts (13/14 of 18; 16/17 of 28; 29/31 of 46; 39 of 46 at h = 0; 7 statements 2, 43, 10, 11, 30, 41, 44) all verified against results/statement_checks.csv. The packet's S2/S3 status_reason says '5 that still disagree are 10, 11, 30, 41, 44', inconsistent with its own 39 of 46; the paper's 7 is correct (packet defect, not paper).

10 of 15 opposite, 5 same, 4 RDD-significant cells verified (results/significance_conclusions.json). Should-fix: Chen's own printed p. 85 (PDF p. 99) already says the RDD PNDE/TNDE CIs at cutoffs 1-2 'indicate that the PNDE and TNDE estimates were significant' (a Type I error) and that MINT and cutoff-3 direct effects 'correctly indicate' non-significance; the paper should say the overgeneralization is between her abstract/p. 143 summary and her own Chapter 4 reading. Verdict and status are unaffected.
Every claim has a row; blocked rows use 'withheld/unavailable', not mismatch.
All seven packet limitations present in order; item 1 is appropriately more hedged than the packet ('evidently ... an inference from her figures').

findings.location: Section 10 item 3 vs p6 Section 4.3 and p4 Section 3.4
findings.finding: Should-fix inconsistency: item 3 says hidden points 'are flagged and not used for verdicts (H3, S2, S3)' and p4 says an occluded marker 'is not used for any verdict', but E4's published value and tolerance include the cutoff-1 point whose status is 'occluded' in results/digitized_rates.csv. Disclosed on p1 caption, p6 and p17. Excluding it leaves the published mean unchanged (0.0627) and the tolerance about .009, so no number or label changes; the limitation wording should carve out this partly hidden point.
H3 image reading, H4 'tentative', S1 zero-estimate partial fit and S5 divisor ambiguity all present and faithful to packet claims[].limitations.
Every number labeled as hers, our simulation/calculation, or an assumption we supplied (Section 7).

'The replay therefore reproduces her printed pipeline, not her published runs'; literal identity claimed only for 'the first block of datasets' (r-reproduction/out-full/literal_check.txt: 1270 datasets, difference 0, RNG state identical). Not overstated.
Scalar summaries and the E4 measurement tolerance are declared as ours and post hoc ('not set in the plan').
See standalone_prose: 'differ only' sentence understates the inferred data difference; should-fix wording.

Chen (2021) cites chen2021: Donna Chen, 'Statistical Mediation Analysis in Regression Discontinuity Design for Causal Inference', doctoral dissertation, University of Nebraska-Lincoln, 2021, digitalcommons.unl.edu/cehsdiss/403 - matches source title page metadata and packet replicated_work.

'biased direct-effect estimates' (source p. 147, 'When bias was present ... a negative value'), 'cover the true value far too rarely' (Table 4.9; p. 150 'systematically fell above the CIs'), 'power for MINT near zero' (p. 121 'All power for MINT is near zero'; p. 148 'never reached the .80 level'), 'tentative minimum of 5,000' (p. 150 'Tentatively, a minimum sample size of 5000 ...'), 'opposite significance conclusions' (abstract p. iii; p. 143). All verified in source/chen2021.pdf.
The paper also records that Chen's abstract/p. 143 say Type I error and power for all five effects reached the criteria, contradicting her MINT statement - verified in source abstract and p. 143.
Contrasts defined against their nulls with units and positive meaning; caption contains 'Descriptive point estimates; not equivalence.'

E1/E2 0.005 (mean of two-decimal printed values; source Tables 4.8-4.9 printed to two decimals), E3 0.01 (difference of two such means), E4 0.0123 measurement (mean reading error 0.01233 of three points, rounded down, post hoc, disclosed). Derivations verified.

Should-fix: 'Monte Carlo standard errors of 0.005-0.02 points' for our E2/E3 means is not recorded in any packet artifact. It is derivable (0.69 points per cell / sqrt(19,200) ~ 0.005 if cells independent; / sqrt(1,280) ~ 0.019 if fully correlated within condition) and does not change any label, but its derivation should be recorded with the evidence.
E4 cell chosen 'after the full results were available' disclosed; magnitude 'larger' and direction 'same' explained as 'about one reading error: small and positive'.

Published 'within [-.10, .10] in only 12.50-18.75% of conditions, with negative bias' = source Table 4.8 (p. 88) and p. 147. Ours 'within [-.05, .05] in 100% of conditions; largest |bias| 0.016' = results/table48_ours.csv (max 0.0155) and summary.json overall_max_abs_bias 0.01551.

Published 'Coverage 24.10-83.99% ...; true value usually above the CI' = source Table 4.9 min/max coverage and p. 150. Ours 'Coverage 94.6-95.6% ...; misses on both sides at similar rates' = results/table49_ours.csv (94.59-95.63; below 1.84-2.71, above 2.52-2.90). E3 reuses E2's text; it still states E3's own finding (above vs both sides). Polish: give the above/below shares in E3.

Published 'MINT power near zero at every sample size; never reaches .80 (Figure 4.28: 0.057-0.068 in this cell)' = source p. 121 / p. 148 and digitized 0.0571-0.0683. Ours '0.836 at n = 500 for ah = .20; at least .97 for ah >= .13 from n = 1,000' = summary.json (0.8361; min 0.9735).

Published = source p. 150 'Tentatively, a minimum sample size of 5000 ...'. Ours = statement_checks.csv n = 5000 summary rows (86.3%, 89.2%; by cutoff 85.7-87.0, 88.3-89.9) and both-zero conservative cells (disagreement_tests.json n5000.both_paths_zero).

H4 is a tentative design recommendation over the whole grid (source p. 150); no single signed contrast represents it. Row shows 'qualitative, no scalar contrast', magnitude and direction 'not established', tolerance 'not applicable' (caption), while the scientific verdict 'partial' is kept separate and supported by shares at each n in Section 4.4 (p7).
The 'not equivalence' note is stated for scalar rows E1-E4; E5's qualitative status is explicit in its row label.
